messages:
maya: FYI: Release builds of sampleapp are intermittently dropping streaming tokens on some devices (OEM HTTP stack conflicts). Debug APK always works.
jon: interesting. repro device?
maya: repro on Pixel 4a (Android 13) and OnePlus 8 (Android 12) with vendor okhttp present. Logs show NoSuchMethodError for okio.Buffer methods in release.
priya: that's usually a proguard/shading problem or classpath mismatch. Do we ship consumer proguard rules in the SDK aar?
maya: aar has proguard.txt but our consumerRules aren't being merged into the app because the app uses an unusual variant setup. I added explicit keep rules and the crash went away.
jon: which keep rules did you add?
maya: small snippet I used:
```
-keep class okhttp3.** { *; }
-keep class okio.** { *; }
-keepclassmembers class okhttp3.internal.** { *; }
```
priya: also check BuildConfig flags. We had one case where a debug logging interceptor remained enabled in release because of a mis-merged constant. That causes extra buffering and sometimes EOFs.
android-oncall: tagging @android-oncall for tracking. Action items: 1) Confirm SDK publishes consumerProguardFiles (ENG-4601). 2) Add CI job that builds release APK + runs streaming integration on emulator/device farm. 3) Short-term: update sampleapp README with proguard snippet and switch the default sample client to a shaded okhttp or explicit connection pool settings.
ci-bot: CI failure: SampleReleaseIntegration - StreamReleaseTest timed out (120s). https://ci.redwood/test/13021
jon: long-term we should consider shading okhttp/okio inside the SDK to avoid OEM-provided platform conflicts. Size tradeoff though.
priya: agreed. I'll file a PR to ensure consumer proguard merging and add a release-mode streaming test.
maya: thanks all. I'll follow up with a minimal repro and link in the ticket. https://git.internal/repro/release-stream-1999999999
